title: The instructions after amrit
hookLine: the initiated are told the banis, the five Ks and the four things to avoid

cards: The amrit has been drunk. It has been sprinkled on the eyes and the hair. The words have been called out and answered.
From the outside, this looks like the end. And still nobody leaves.
One of the five turns to the newly initiated and starts to speak, slowly, the way you'd give directions to someone who has to remember them without a map.
Before anyone walks out of that quiet room, the promise gets spelled out, piece by piece, out loud. Nothing is left in small print.

teach.h: A NEW FAMILY: THE GURU'S HOUSEHOLD.
teach.b: The Sikh Rehat Maryada sets out what is said. In paraphrase, four parts. First, a new family.
The initiated are told that from today they're born into the Guru's household: Guru Gobind Singh their spiritual father, Mata Sahib Kaur their spiritual mother, Anandpur their home.
Whatever caste or clan they came from is left behind; they are one family with every Sikh of the Khalsa.
Second, the daily banis, morning, evening and night, prayers this path walked through not long ago: Japji and Jaap among them at dawn, Rehras at evening, Kirtan Sohila before sleep.
Third, the five Ks: kesh, uncut hair; kangha, the comb; kara, the steel bracelet; kachhera, the shorts worn underneath; and kirpan, the sword.

teach.h: THE FIVE Ks, KEPT ON THE BODY.
teach.b: Each is kept on the body.

The code calls them kurahits and names four: dishonoring the hair by cutting it; eating the meat of an animal killed in the ritual way the code calls kutha; sexual contact with anyone other than one's spouse; and using tobacco.
Someone who commits one must come back and take amrit again. Look at the order.
Family comes first: who you belong to, then what you do. The rules hang on the relationship, not the other way round.
And it's all said aloud, in the Guru's presence, before the five, so nobody can say later they weren't told.
These are the promises of those who take amrit; as this path said long ago, there are many ways of being Sikh, and every seeker is welcome.

how: After amrit is given, one of the five explains the rehat to the newly initiated: their new spiritual family, the daily banis, the five Ks and the four kurahits to avoid, as the Sikh Rehat Maryada lays out.

practice: Bring to mind one promise you've already made, to a person, to yourself, or to God if you pray, and find the plain words for it, short enough to fit on a sticky note.
Say it once in your head, slowly, as if someone were listening for every word, and notice whether the plain version feels heavier or lighter than the vague one.

wordCard.voice: The instructions after amrit. The new Khalsa family, the daily banis, the five Ks and the four things to avoid, spoken aloud before anyone leaves. Today's word.

orig.note: Punjabi: a grave breach of the rehat. the code names four.

carryVoice: Your line: what is promised. Not a vague feeling, but words that are specific, spoken and heard. Until tomorrow.
